plan.statement: Room areas are measured to wall centerlines; net floor areas are smaller.

plan.basis: typical values for a first layout, not a regulation
plan.statement: Floor-to-floor height 3 m; split levels step in half storeys of 1.5 m; walls 2.8 m high.

plan.basis: typical thicknesses for a first layout
plan.statement: Exterior and retaining walls 0.3 m, partitions 0.15 m thick; no structural design has been done.
Plan grid: u axis along the parcel edge nearest road road-uphill.
Entry level set at the mean surveyed ground along the road-side face (11.70 m local), interpolated from the survey TIN (inferred).
Stair risers at most 0.18 m with 0.28 m goings; typical comfortable geometry, not checked against any code.

plan.basis: typical car length plus clearance; not in the program
plan.statement: A garage needs at least 5.4 m depth for a car.
The plan is kept inside the buildable envelope (synthetic setbacks (3 m road side, 2 m sides, 3 m rear) invented for the example; not a zoning rule).
Level elevations, earth contact and retaining walls are inferred by linear interpolation of the surveyed points; ground between survey points is not verified.

program.statement: Rooms without a size from you use typical sizes for a first layout: Entrance hall 6 m², Living room 25 m², Kitchen 12 m², Dining 14 m², Main bedroom 15 m², Child's bedroom 1 11 m², Child's bedroom 2 11 m², En-suite bathroom 5 m², Bathroom 1 6 m², Study 1 9 m², Garage 36 m², Laundry 6 m², Plant / technical room 4 m², Stair 10 m², Terrace 16 m². These are not building-code minimums; no local rules are loaded.

program.basis: Surveyed site relief and slope indicate steep hillside construction.
program.statement: Steep hillside terrain requires split-level or stepped massing, road-level access coordination, excavation, retaining walls, slope drainage, and structural engineering review; the full parcel area cannot be assumed buildable.
